function: DNN maps channels to transmit beamformer powers and RIS phase shifts (MMSE directions) maximizing weighted sum rate; a CV module selects which RIS to activate (p. 3, 4)
system: Multi-RIS multi-user MISO: NT=8 transmit antennas, K=4 users, 2L=6 passive reflecting RISs with N=8 elements each, one activated at a time; band not stated (p. 2, 5)
method: Fully connected DNN (ReLU, batch normalization, sigmoid outputs), unsupervised training on negative weighted sum rate with Adam; CV module is an SSD with VGG16 backbone (p. 3, 4)
data_channel: DNN: 100,000 unlabeled training samples; 1,000 test samples labeled by AO (25 or 50 iterations); channel generation model not specified; CV trained on random top views (p. 5)
test_conditions: Single scenario: 2L=6, N=8, NT=8, K=4, path-loss-to-noise ratio 20 dB; test set of 1,000 samples; no other scenario reported (p. 5)
baselines: Classical: alternating-optimization (AO) algorithm with 25 or 50 iterations; no learned baseline; CV module has no comparison (p. 5)
metrics: Average weighted sum rate (bit/s/Hz), average inference time, and CV module frame rate of 11 FPS (p. 5)
complexity: Order O(sum_g (a_{g+1} a_g^2 + a_{g+1}) + (K+N)(1 + a_{G+1}^2)); DNN inference 0.02 ms versus 69.8 s and 118.9 s for AO 25 and AO 50 (p. 4, 5)
q1_support: p. 5: "The DNN is trained on a set of 100, 000 unlabeled samples". Not met: the channels are not tied to any named standardized model or measured data; the paper defines only an obstacle-dependent effective path loss (p. 2).
q2_support: p. 5: "respectively set by 2L = 6, N = 8, NT = 8, and K = 4". Not met: a single scenario is simulated and the test set is a set of labeled samples of it; no other number of RISs, elements, antennas or users is tested.
q3_support: p. 5: "the result of 25 iterations via the AO-based algorithm (denoted by AO 25)". Not met: Table I compares the DNN only with the classical AO algorithm (25 and 50 iterations); the DNN designs of refs. [9]-[11] are cited on p. 1 but not compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "DNN-enabled transmit design is on the order of"; p. 5: "the inference speed of DNN is one million faster than the AO-based algorithm"
q5_support: p. 5: "Our implementation is developed using Python 3.9.18 with Pytorch 2.2.0". Not met: no code or data link, DOI or release statement is given; the datasets are generated by the authors.
notes: Included as area 3: the DNN designs the beamformers and RIS phase shifts; the CV module only selects which RIS to activate, through a closed-form rule on the detected positions (p. 3). The PDF is the arXiv v1 preprint (arXiv:2404.11836v1, p. 1) and carries no DOI, so the match with the DOI rests on the file name. The paper does not say how H, h_k and g_k are generated. Table I gives AO inference times of 69.8 s and 118.9 s against 0.02 ms for the DNN (p. 5). Pages are file pages.
